title: Planning, todos and agent modes
summary: Two Harness context providers give the agent a durable to-do list and a plan or execute operating mode. The list is injected before each run so work can resume. They record progress but do not re-invoke the agent.
useIf: A task spans many steps or sessions and you want visible progress and a human review point before autonomous work.
avoidIf: The task fits one short run, or the steps must follow a fixed order that you can encode as a workflow.

explain.md: The **todo provider** (`TodoProvider`) stores work items and exposes five model-facing tools: `todos_add`, `todos_complete` (with a completion reason), `todos_remove`, `todos_get_remaining` and `todos_get_all`. It injects the current list before each run, so the agent can pick up outstanding work [[tr8]].

The **agent mode provider** (`AgentModeProvider`) keeps the current mode in the session and exposes `mode_get` and `mode_set`. Two modes are built in: **plan** (interactive: analyse, create todos, ask clarifying questions, present a plan and ask before changing mode) and **execute** (autonomous: work through the plan, make reasonable choices when details are ambiguous, mark todos complete). Applications can switch mode directly, which queues a one-time mode-change notice for the next run [[tr8]].

**Two honest limits.** The plan-to-execute confirmation is an instruction to the model, not a tool-approval request, and the todo and mode tools need no approval; if your host must enforce permission, change the mode from application code after you obtain it. And todo tracking does not re-invoke the agent: pair it with a bounded loop (see looping) when execute mode should continue until every todo is done [[tr8]].

explain.title: Mode lifecycle
explain.alt: The agent starts in plan mode, loops while clarifying and adding todos, moves to execute mode when the human approves, works through todos and ends when all are done.
explain.src:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> plan
  plan --> plan: clarify and add todos
  plan --> execute: human approves
  execute --> execute: work the todos
  execute --> [*]: all todos done

blocks.code:
from agent_framework import (create_harness_agent, TodoProvider, TodoFileStore,
    AgentModeProvider, set_agent_mode, todos_remaining, todos_remaining_message)

todo = TodoProvider(store=TodoFileStore('./todo-state'))
mode = AgentModeProvider(default_mode='plan')
agent = create_harness_agent(
    client=client, todo_provider=todo, mode_provider=mode,
    loop_should_continue=todos_remaining(looping_modes=['execute']),
    loop_next_message=todos_remaining_message,
    loop_max_iterations=10,
)
session = agent.create_session()

# after the human approves the plan:
set_agent_mode(session, 'execute', source_id=mode.source_id,
               available_modes=mode.available_modes)

whereToUse: Research and analysis agents that produce a plan a person reviews before work starts
Coding or migration agents that need a visible checklist across many tool calls
Resumable work: todos persist in the session (.NET `StateBag`, Python `TodoSessionStore` by default)
UIs that show progress by reading the todo list and the current mode

use: The task has many steps and the model otherwise loses track
A human should agree the plan before autonomous execution
You want progress that survives session restore
avoid: Short tasks: the extra tools and instructions are overhead
You need an enforced gate before execute mode: do it in application code, not model instructions
The steps are a fixed pipeline: encode them as workflow edges
flips: The todo list must live outside the session payload: use `TodoFileStore` or a custom `TodoStore` (Python)
You supply your own mode UI: hide the built-in tools with `expose_mode_set=False` and `expose_mode_get=False`, and call `set_agent_mode(..., notify=False)` from your tool

pitfalls.symptom: The agent stops with todos still open
pitfalls.cause: Todo tracking does not re-invoke the agent
pitfalls.fix: Add a bounded loop with a todo evaluator, limited to execute mode

pitfalls.symptom: Plan mode instructions mention file memory but the agent cannot write the plan
pitfalls.cause: A manually composed agent has no file-memory tools; the default plan instructions write the plan to file memory
pitfalls.fix: Add a memory provider or customise the mode instructions

pitfalls.symptom: The model switches to execute without permission
pitfalls.cause: The confirmation is an instruction, not a control; `mode_set` has no approval
pitfalls.fix: Hide `mode_set` and change mode from application code after the human approves

scenarios.title: Plan review before a risky migration
scenarios.situation: A coding agent will refactor a service. The lead wants to read the plan first. Once approved the agent should run alone for up to an hour.
unknowns: Must the model be unable to start executing early?
Do any tools need approval in execute mode?
scenarios.question: How do you wire it?

options.name: Plan mode by default, hide `mode_set`, flip to execute from your UI after approval, loop on todos with a cap
options.why: The gate is enforced in application code, todos track progress and the loop caps the run.
options.tradeoff: You build the UI and the loop is experimental.

options.name: Leave the built-in `mode_set` tool and trust the model to ask first
options.tradeoff: The confirmation is an instruction, so the model could switch without approval.

options.name: A workflow with a plan node and an execute node
options.why: The execute step is open-ended, so a fixed graph adds little.
options.tradeoff: Right when planning and execution are separate, auditable stages.

flips.if: The execute phase calls irreversible tools
flips.then: Keep per-call tool approval on those tools even in execute mode.

flips.if: Plans must be stored for audit
flips.then: Persist the todo list with a file or custom store, not only the session.

scenarios.takeaway: A mode is a hint to the model. A gate that matters belongs in your code.

scenarios.title: Weekly report generator
scenarios.situation: A scheduled job asks an agent to compile a weekly report from three data sources. The steps are always the same and nobody reviews a plan.
unknowns: How long does a run take?
scenarios.question: Do you use todos and modes?

options.name: No: build a short workflow or a plain agent with the steps in its instructions
options.why: Fixed steps need no discovered plan, and todo and mode tools add tokens.

options.name: Harness with todos and execute mode only
Magentic orchestration for planning
options.why: Planning cost with no unknown path to plan.

flips.if: Source count and order vary per customer
flips.then: Use the Harness so the agent builds the todo list per run.

flips.if: The report must pass an audit of step order
flips.then: Use a workflow with explicit edges.

scenarios.takeaway: Planning tools earn their cost only when the plan is not known in advance.

quiz.q: Match each tool to its provider role.

pairs.r: Marks items done with a reason
Deletes items that no longer matter

quiz.explain: The todo provider exposes add, complete, remove, get remaining and get all. The mode provider exposes `mode_get` and `mode_set`.

quiz.q: You need the agent to keep working in execute mode until every todo is complete. What is required beyond the todo provider?
options: Nothing: the todo provider re-invokes the agent
A second agent that polls the list
A bounded agent loop with a todo-completion condition
quiz.explain: Todo tracking records progress but does not re-invoke the agent. Pair it with `LoopAgent` or `AgentLoopMiddleware` and a todo evaluator, with a maximum.

flashcards.front: What are the two built-in agent modes?
flashcards.back: `plan` (interactive: analyse, todos, clarify, present plan) and `execute` (autonomous: work the plan, mark todos complete).

flashcards.front: Is plan-to-execute confirmation enforced by the framework?
flashcards.back: No. It is an instruction to the model; the mode and todo tools need no approval. Enforce gates from application code.
